common_name: Summer Skies Butterfly Bush (Variegated Blue-Purple Buddleja)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; the variegated foliage holds its gold-and-green pattern best with consistent sun exposure.

directions: Summer Skies pairs the familiar pale violet-blue, honey-scented flower spikes of a standard-size Buddleja with leaves edged in bright yellow over a mid-dark green center, so the shrub reads as a bright accent even between bloom flushes. Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun, since the variegation can revert to plain green in heavy shade and the foliage can scorch if the soil stays too wet. Cut the entire plant back hard to 12-18 inches in late winter, as flowers and the best-colored new leaves both come from current-season wood. Deadhead through summer to keep fresh spikes forming and to prevent the plant from putting energy into seed instead of repeat bloom.
sources: US Plant Patent USPP22465P2 (Mark Brand/William Smith, University of Connecticut)

common_name: Darkest Night Butterfly Bush (Deep Royal Purple Buddleja with Burnt Orange Throats)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; Darkest Night's mid-size, well-behaved frame fits mixed borders without the sprawl of older large davidii selections.

directions: Darkest Night carries dark royal purple flower spikes with contrasting burnt-orange throats, among the deepest, most saturated purple tones yet bred into the Buddleja ColorChoice line, held upright and slightly outward-facing against gray-green foliage. Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun, since lean conditions keep the habit tight and heavily flowered rather than lax and floppy. Cut the whole plant back hard in late winter, as bloom forms only on new season's wood and this annual renewal is what keeps the mid-size, well-behaved habit the cultivar is bred for. Its fragrant blooms draw butterflies and hummingbirds from early summer into fall and stand out strongly against paler neighboring plantings.
sources: US Plant Patent USPP37501P2 (Megan Mathey, Spring Meadow Nursery)

common_name: Lo & Behold Ruby Chip Butterfly Bush (Dwarf Sterile Dark Red-Purple Buddleja)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; Ruby Chip brings one of the deepest flower colors yet to the dwarf Lo & Behold series.

directions: Ruby Chip joins the sterile Lo & Behold series with dark red-purple flowers, carried in dense spikes on a tidy, mounded frame scaled for small gardens. Because its patent record notes no observed seed or fruit development, the plant channels its energy into repeated bloom flushes from summer into fall rather than seed production, and needs no deadheading to keep flowering. Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun, and cut the entire plant back hard in late winter to renew flowering wood and preserve its compact, space-saving shape. Its small footprint and intense color make it a strong choice for mixed containers and tight border spots where full-size butterfly bush cultivars would overwhelm neighboring plants.
sources: US Plant Patent USPP32399P2 (Megan Mathey, Spring Meadow Nursery)

common_name: Pugster Sorbet Butterfly Bush (Dwarf Lavender-to-Cream Bicolor Buddleja)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; Pugster Sorbet sets no viable seed, so it stays tidy and non-invasive without deadheading.

directions: Pugster Sorbet opens flower buds in lavender that mature to cream with a contrasting orange throat, giving each cluster a two-toned, sorbet-like blend of color across the bloom. Plant in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun, since excess fertility or shade produces loose, sparsely flowered growth. It is part of the seedless In-Check breeding line, so it never sets viable seed and needs no deadheading to keep blooming from summer through fall. Cut the entire plant back hard in late winter to renew flowering wood and keep its tidy, rounded, deer- and rabbit-resistant habit compact.
sources: US Plant Patent USPP37502P2 (Megan Mathey, Spring Meadow Nursery)
